references.text: Describes the Day of Atonement as a holy day of rest (Sabbath) where the people must humble themselves, the same theme as in Leviticus 23:32
The introduction to the Day of Atonement describing that there shall be a holy assembly where the people must humble themselves and do no work
Mentions the tenth day of the seventh month and that the Jubilee year is to begin on the Day of Atonement
Shows the same time reckoning 'from evening to evening' used to define the duration of a day
Defines the Sabbath as a day of rest, and the expression 'Sabbath sabbaton' (complete rest) is also used here
Parallel text about the Day of Atonement on the tenth day of the seventh month, with a command to humble oneself and not work
Isaiah discusses the meaning of humbling oneself (fasting), which is central to the practice of the Day of Atonement
Refers to 'the Fast' as the Day of Atonement, showing that this day was still observed in New Testament times
Mentions the Day of Atonement in the Old Testament and how the high priest entered the Most Holy Place once a year
